steps: WHAT YOU NEED
Ableton Live 12.4 or later, Suite edition (Max for Live is built in). No plug-ins.
Optional: an Arturia KeyLab 49 mk3; everything also works with the mouse
For the in-ear mix: an audio interface with 4 outputs
Chrome or Edge, for the /live/ backup
Live 12.4 Suite is open
DOWNLOAD AND UNZIP
Press DOWNLOAD THE PROJECT (0.9 GB)
Unzip it anywhere and keep the folders together; an SSD is best
Optional: check the download with the SHA-256 shown in the transfer panel, or run  shasum -a 256 -c CHECKSUMS.txt  inside each folder
you have ARCHIVE_404 Live Project and ERROR 404 Instruments Project
OPEN THE SET
Double-click ARCHIVE_404 Live.als
Arrangement view: 20 songs, 188 locators, a tempo lane that follows every beat
If Live asks for missing files, the unzip went wrong: unzip again
the SETLIST track shows 20 coloured song blocks
AUDIO SETTINGS
Settings › Audio: your interface, 48 kHz, buffer 128 (64 if your voice feels late)
Outputs 1/2 = the PA. Outputs 3/4 = your ears: click, spoken cues, guide vocal
Main › Cue Out = 3/4, so the click never reaches the PA
you hear the set on the PA and nothing else
MIDI SETTINGS
Settings › Link, Tempo & MIDI: Control Surface 1 = KeyLab_mk3 (its DAW ports)
KeyLab 49 mk3 (MIDI) port: Track ON and Remote ON
Audio MIDI Setup › Window › Show MIDI Studio › IAC Driver › Device is online
Back in Live, IAC Driver (Bus 1) has two rows: on the OUT row, Track ON
the OUT row of IAC Driver shows Track ON
MIC AND TUNER
Mic into input 1: the MIC track already monitors IN
TUNE is Ableton's Auto Shift (hard tune); its key changes with every song by itself
Sing a line: the guide vocal drops 12 dB under you and comes back 0.4 s after you stop
the GUIDE VOX meter dips when you sing
THE KEYLAB
Pads in Arturia mode: 1–6 = this song's vocal chops, 7–12 = one-shots
Lowest keys C, C♯, D = REPEAT, SKIP, NEXT SONG, landing on the next bar
Encoders 1–8 = the E404 FX macros, 9 = the mic's echo throw; faders = the mix
Every control is drawn in THE KEYLAB below, and TEST YOUR RIG checks them
pad 1 plays a vocal chop
PRE-SHOW CHECK
Click the SETLIST track, then CHECK on the E404 SHOW device
Every line green: data, position feed, REC, tuner, tape stop, click, 48 kHz
PROMPTER opens the big lyric window for a second screen
CHECK shows all green
THE BACKUP
In Chrome, open /live/ and enter the key
Menu › CONTROL › ABLETON STANDBY: the page follows Ableton, silent
If Ableton stops, the bar turns amber: TAKE OVER carries on from the same spot
the standby bar counts along with Ableton
moves: Back to the start of this section, landing on the next bar.
On to the next section, landing on the next bar.
Straight to the next song, landing on the next bar.

flow.mic: Your voice: input 1 → TUNE (Auto Shift) → GRIT → DOUBLER → the PA. A PLATE send and the ECHO THROW (encoder 9) sit on the side.
flow.duck: The duck: your mic keys a gate on GUIDE VOX. While you sing, the recorded vocal drops 12 dB; 0.4 s after you stop, it's back to cover you.
flow.pads: Pads: the KeyLab's pads on channel 10 play the song's chops and the one-shots into the SONG group, so ROLL, TAPE STOP and the rest catch them.
flow.ears: In-ears: the click (Live's metronome on the Cue out), the spoken cues and the full guide vocal go to outputs 3/4 only, never the PA.
flow.feed: Backup: the E404 SHOW device sends the playhead over the Mac's IAC bus; /live/ in Chrome follows it, silent, ready to TAKE OVER.

trouble: In Live's Settings › Link, Tempo & MIDI, IAC Driver (Bus 1) has two rows. Switch Track ON on the OUT row, then press CHECK again. If there's no IAC row at all, switch the IAC Driver on in Audio MIDI Setup first.
The ears are on outputs 3/4. A 2-output interface has none: use a 4-output interface, or an aggregate device in Audio MIDI Setup.
Put the KeyLab's pads in Arturia mode (not DAW). VOX PADS and KIT PADS listen to channel 10 only, so the keys can never fire them.
THE GUIDE DOESN'T DROP WHEN I SING
Raise your mic gain, or lower the threshold of DUCK UNDER MIC on GUIDE VOX until it reacts to your voice but not to the room.
Lower the buffer to 64 in Settings › Audio. Auto Shift adds very little delay; the buffer is usually the cause.
Run CHECK in Ableton (POSITION FEED must read OK · Ch. 16), use Chrome or Edge, and allow MIDI when Chrome asks.
LIVE SAYS IT CAN'T OPEN THE SET
The set needs Live 12.4 or later, Suite edition. Earlier versions can't read it.
pre: KEYLAB ON · PADS IN ARTURIA MODE
IAC ON · TRACK ON ITS OUT ROW
MIC · GUIDE VOX DIPS WHEN YOU SING
EARS ON 3/4 · CLICK AND CUES HEARD
facts: tempo points, one per analysed beat: the approved audio plays untouched while the grid sits on the music
locators: every song and section, so REPEAT and SKIP land where you expect
vocal chops cut on word timings, six per song, swapping at every changeover
guitar hits behind CHUG: four tones, round robin, two velocity layers, all from the album
hand edits: rebuild after any timing change and the set, the prompter and /live/ still agree

instruments.name: CHUG
instruments.text: The album's drop-tuned chugs, cut at every guitar note in its MIDI. Low keys chug, pitched per key, with round robin so fast 16ths never machine-gun; play harder for the sharper picks.
keys: 12 ONE-BAR RIFFS · HOLD TO LOOP, AT YOUR TEMPO

instruments.name: GLITCH VOX
instruments.text: Lead, backing and gang syllables, each pitch-checked and fine-tuned to its note. Pick a chop with CHOP; every key then plays it at exactly that note.
keys: THE CHOSEN CHOP AT THE NOTE YOU PLAY

instruments.name: SUB 404
instruments.text: A clean, mono sine sub that stays in tune on every key, with the album's own bass notes looped underneath as a grit layer through Roar and OTT.

instruments.name: KIT 404
instruments.text: Kick, rim, snare, clap, toms, hats, 808 and crash from eight songs' drum stems, laid out the same way in every octave. The KeyLab's octave buttons pick which four kits are under your hands.
keys: C KICK · D SNARE · D♯ CLAP · F♯ HAT · A OPEN HAT · A♯ 808 · B CRASH

instruments.name: ATMOS
instruments.text: Held chords from the strings, synths and keys, stretched in Simpler's Texture mode into pads that last as long as you hold them. Play one key for the whole chord.
keys: THE CHORD, ROOTED ON THE KEY YOU PLAY
